tower_sealed.evidence: shut since the barges stopped coming, its gates chained and its windows boarded ... Nobody in town remembered why Engineer Maren Pool had sealed it so carefully
tower_sealed.note: "sealed it so carefully" plus the pinned puzzle makes the seal read as deliberate rather than accidental.

challenge_posted.evidence: somebody had pinned a fresh sheet of paper to the door anyway: rows of small flags ... arranged like a puzzle waiting for the right eyes

friends_committed_together.evidence: They looked at each other and nodded. Together, then.

challenge_accepted.evidence: This was Engineer Pool's puzzle, and Pool had never made anything without a reason, so tearing the note down or guessing wildly felt like the wrong kind of answer

patience_proven.evidence: It had taken the better part of an hour ... but the note had rewarded exactly the kind of patience it demanded
patience_proven.note: The decode is shown line by line on the page: flags to numbers, add, carry past twelve.

route_named_by_note.evidence: the line resolved into an address more than a riddle: the dry culvert under the towpath, the one that ran dry at low water since the new channel opened
route_named_by_note.note: A specific way in is named; "what waits there" is covered only by the culvert being dry and passable, which is thin but sufficient.

self_reliance_shown.evidence: a hatch gave a groan and swung open ... Bel felt the stiff side door shift under her palm at the same moment ... They had found that out themselves
self_reliance_shown.note: Both the high way (hatch) and the low way (side door) are opened, and the node insists no note helped.

keeper_tested_them.evidence: Issa took her time looking them over, the kind of look that weighs more than it says ... 'Asking straight is half the test, and you just passed it.'

keeper_offer_earned.evidence: 'Come on, then. I'll row you across myself.'
keeper_offer_earned.note: The way in is offered outright; the maker half arrives as volunteered knowledge ('Pool built that place to test people, not keep them out') rather than an explicit offer to tell more.

logic_earned.evidence: they now had proof, engraved in stone, that they understood how the tide arithmetic actually worked, not just how to copy it once

maker_motive_understood.evidence: she started building little tests into everything ... to find the ones who'd actually take care of what they were given ... 'She wasn't unkind. Just particular.'
maker_motive_understood.note: Care and finder-selection are explicit; the decades-ago timeframe is implied by the past-tense history rather than stated.

past_the_seal.evidence: Otto caught the sill, hauled himself through ... They dropped through one after another onto the winch-loft floor, dusty and grinning, properly inside at last
Inside, the lock-house smelled of rope oil and cold stone, and the tide engine breathed somewhere below

trial_rooms_known.evidence: Four ways led off the entry hall, each one plainly a test of its own kind. A spiral stair ... a room lined with charts and ledgers ... a narrow catwalk ... a ladder dropped down into a basement
trial_rooms_known.note: Climb, study, crossing and descent all named and sensory; none is ranked.

logic_earned.evidence: the weir gates below, sluicing in a steady run, long, long, short, long, long, short ... It matched the flags on the door exactly ... they had the pattern memorized cold
logic_earned.note: What is earned is a rhythm that matches the door's flags, not the moon-day-plus-posted-hour, carry-past-twelve arithmetic the dial actually tests. A reader who came up the stairs without reading the note carries a memorized rhythm and no way to convert it, so the grasp is not yet working for the dial. The node's own constraint (hint sufficient on its own) is not met.

logic_earned.evidence: hoist levers along the back wall, each stamped with an hour, one through twelve, their handles worn bright wherever a pull lined up with today's moon day carried past twelve
logic_earned.note: The wear pattern states the full rule, so the dial is attemptable from this room alone.

archive_beckons.evidence: stacked to the ceiling with river charts, decades of them ... Bel could have stayed a week just tracing channels that didn't exist anymore
archive_beckons.note: The pull is honest and the stay-or-press-on question is live in the choices.

logic_earned.evidence: Depth figures were stamped up the entrance posts, climbing the same way the hoists carried, a number for every step in
logic_earned.note: The only link to the cipher is an oblique comparison to the hoists, which live in a different room this path never visits, and the figures are used for pacing in the dark rather than understood. Nothing here states or demonstrates the carry-past-twelve rule, and no moment of grasping it occurs.

crossing_dares_them.evidence: Of the four rooms, this one didn't bother hiding what it was asking: cross, or don't

reward_glimpsed.evidence: something glinting on a shelf at the far side, small and deliberately placed, clearly set aside for whoever proved brave enough to reach it

logic_earned.evidence: its margins crowded with scrawled sums, moon days added to hours, carried past twelve ... Ash traced the working with one finger until it made sense

at_the_dial.evidence: The great tide board took up most of the top room: a broad brass dial, ringed with twelve hour-marks ... Whoever answered correctly would feel the mechanism agree
at_the_dial.note: The examiner role is explicit in how the board responds to right answers and to force.

dial_test_live.evidence: A hand-lettered plate beneath both rings spelled it out plainly ... add the moon day to the posted hour, carry past twelve, and set the hands there
dial_test_live.note: What to set is stated plainly by the dial's own plate. The other half, that guessing has a cost, is not on the markings: it is narration that the board 'gave no sign that hoping had ever once worked,' which is futility, not a cost. The stated cost belongs to forcing, a different bet.

test_passed.evidence: the whole board gave a firm, satisfied click ... Whatever this trial had wanted from them, it had just admitted they'd given it
test_passed.note: The sum is worked on the page from the plate and the posted slip, so it holds on paths that never read the note.

test_forced.evidence: Otto put both hands on the crank and heaved without waiting on any sum ... It just locked, hands frozen half a turn short, gears grinding to a dead stop

second_test_found.evidence: Behind it sat a second, smaller plate, its own miniature ring of hour-marks no wider than a coin ... just condensed

sanctum_entered.evidence: Past the seam, the strongroom was small and dry, built to survive any flood the river ever threw at it
sanctum_entered.note: Written as already through, without naming which test opened it.

sanctum_seen.evidence: Maren Pool's last workbook sat open on a stand, ending mid-page in a letter ... a model of the lock-house itself ... a rank of narrow pipes
sanctum_seen.note: Letter plus modest things are all seen; that they are meant for everyone is carried by 'keep the river honest' and 'Nothing here was worth carrying off,' implied rather than stated.

composure_kept.evidence: nobody wanted to leave, and the tide board upstairs sat untouched and unbothered by it
composure_kept.note: Staying is framed as absorption, never as failure or shaming.

trial_reopens.evidence: The trial would still be there tomorrow, patient as everything else Pool had built, and so would they

composure_kept.evidence: They didn't call it giving up ... nobody looked over their shoulder twice
composure_kept.note: Otto's swallowed argument reads as agreement, not quarrel or shame.

trial_reopens.evidence: The lock-house wasn't going anywhere, and neither was that shelf

composure_kept.evidence: 'That old thing hates being spun,' she said, not unkindly ... She waited while they collected themselves, in no hurry to send them off scolded

trial_reopens.evidence: The board sat still and patient behind her, exactly as unsolved as it had been five minutes earlier, waiting for someone willing to work it out properly

composure_kept.evidence: 'It's not us,' Ash said, more statement than question, and Otto had to agree
composure_kept.note: No blame lands on whoever forced it; they leave planning the retake.

trial_reopens.evidence: The dial stayed latched and settled, exactly as they'd found it, while Bel, Otto, and Ash started down the stairs already comparing notes on what a proper toolkit for a return trip ought to hold
trial_reopens.note: Nothing is used up and a second attempt is explicitly planned, though the same paragraph first has the gears 'locking solid again,' which sits awkwardly against 'exactly as they'd found it.'

workshop_found.evidence: up into a narrow room tucked under the roofline ... a little garden of reeds ... fed drop by drop from a cistern rigged decades ago and somehow, impossibly, still dripping true
workshop_found.note: Reached from behind the hidden plate, and alive rather than preserved.

stewardship_earned.evidence: the model gate had three new fittings it hadn't had an hour before, and three new hands that already knew where the fourth one went
stewardship_earned.note: The ongoing role is shown by their taking up the unfinished work and knowing the next piece, rather than being named as a duty; the continuation is unmistakable.

trust_bond_formed.evidence: Otto found the next piece almost by instinct, and Ash the one after that
trust_bond_formed.note: The wordless three-way work gestures at a bond, but nothing in the node frames the shared trial as having forged a trust between them, or as lasting. The node's attention is on the room and the work.

passing_made_public.evidence: By the next tide, the whole of Eelgate knew three kids had cracked Pool's old test, and the harbor master rang the flood pipes' six notes off the strongroom wall

test_passed.evidence: the whole of Eelgate knew three kids had cracked Pool's old test
test_passed.note: Established by this node rather than carried in, which matters because two of the three routes into n_vault (the jam remedy and the hidden panel) never passed the dial on its own terms.

maker_motive_understood.evidence: this lock-house was never meant to guard treasure, only to sort out who could be trusted with the machinery that kept the river honest
maker_motive_understood.note: Stated by the letter itself, so it holds on paths that never met the keeper.

trust_bond_formed.evidence: Bel, Otto, and Ash looked at each other, not needing to say anything
trust_bond_formed.note: One line of wordless understanding is all the friends get; the trust the node actually dramatizes is Issa's trust in them (the spare key), which is keeper trust, not a lasting bond among the three.

passing_kept_private.evidence: 'Nobody else needs to know we did this,' Bel said, and it wasn't a question
passing_kept_private.note: Reads as guardianship: the letter and pipes are left, the model returned, the panel resealed.

trust_bond_formed.evidence: shook on it right there on the towpath, solemn as a courtroom, and then ruined the moment laughing about who'd flinched first crossing the seam
trust_bond_formed.note: A sworn pact over the keepsake, with the ease of old friends behind it.

record_set_straight.evidence: Otto handed the model back without being asked twice ... just waited while he returned it to its shelf, exactly where it belonged
record_set_straight.note: Owning it is done by action in front of the keeper, without excuse, after his own 'It's not stealing' convinces nobody.

keeper_intervenes.evidence: They made it as far as the winch loft before Warden Issa met them on the ladder, arms crossed, entirely unsurprised

composure_kept.evidence: Issa didn't make a speech out of it ... 'Come back and do it properly sometime,'
composure_kept.note: Firm, brief, no lecture and no shaming.

trial_reopens.evidence: 'Come back and do it properly sometime,' she said, already heading down the ladder
